title: The page builder's model and a built page's render
grade_reasons: The base is sound and partly held: a stored page is 340 bytes a block, blocks and rows are capped, interactive parts load where drawn, and one script budget exists. But every storefront document carries the layout twice (27,070 bytes, 27 to 39% of its payload: I re-ran the script on four captures), one publish makes all 261 built pages of a store stale, 45 built entries keep every page of the store, the owner filter reads 59,973 rows to return 27, and no budget sees a document. It is not a D because the reads are cached and tagged and the second layout is about 1 KB on the wire; it is not a B because none of the large causes is gone.
verdict_on_bar: Kept: one layout per document; an index scan of 27 rows for 27; the page reader at 130 source files (I re-ran the walk: the three imports a reader needs reach 104, so 130 is tight, and the planner's 400 would be a B); Orbit's home at 11,100 bytes stored; the product page's entry at 297,000; the editor's words at 130,000. Tightened in seven places. (1) /om-oss at most 80,000 bytes, not 85,000: the copy is 30,688 bytes as written into the document, so the sum is 79,819, and about 78,000 with each sheet drawn once. (2) The whole-list read on at most 3 lines, not 14. I read the four callers the findings would leave: Kaizena Flow's two static-params functions keep slugs, the admin's search page keeps a slug and a title (search/page.tsx:147), and the feed reads every article of a blog to print 50. None draws every body. (3) Every statement that selects the document of several pages is named with its reason. A rough scan finds about 20 in 17 files; the findings name 5. (4) A body-only publish is proved by its effect (other pages stay cache hits), not by one stubbed call. The steward's count of places that refresh the store-wide tag is dropped as a measure: the fix keeps those places for a changed title, so the count cannot fall. (5) The steward's tolerance, 'a missed fact is stale for at most an hour', is false once step 2.15 gives tagged reads a week; the bar now says which reads keep the hour. (6) A recommending grid loads at most 140,000 bytes after its answer, not 335,000: 335,000 is the figure with zod and the page model still in. And parts are held by name, because 3% of a store page's first scripts is 18,000 to 21,000 bytes, more than the cart's forms (18,876) that slipped in on 10 November. (7) The renderer is in the bar, not only the reader: page-article.tsx reaches 1,396 source files, and still 1,392 with pages.ts taken away, so a lean page-reads.ts alone changes nothing a page render loads. Also added: the owner filter is tested for Kaizena Flow's own rows (store_id is null), the editor's words must be 90% read, and measures 1 and 5 must hold on a themed store, where no figure exists today. Loosened in two places. '0 bytes reachable only through a not-found copy' becomes 'under 2,000 bytes of identical rows': the router keeps the store's 404 words (919 bytes today). 'Each stylesheet once per document' becomes twice, once in the HTML and once in React's payload: that is the framework's floor, and the breakpoint sheet differs per store, so it cannot move to the shared stylesheet. Not measurable as written: '0 built entries keep the page list' and '3 of 261' rest on a scratch script no step puts in the repo; '3 documents on a cold render' has no test that counts documents; '0 parts outside the keep-list' has no check, because the keep-list is prose. The parse time has a bench and no held test: accepted, since measure 2 holds how many documents are parsed. AMENDED BY THE PANEL'S CRITIC, so that one thing has one number in every area: 8: interface text in the editor's document: at most 1.1 times the groups the editor's parts name at first paint, by the same scan; 130,000 bytes inline stays.

measures.name: Copies of the store's layout in one storefront document
measures.today: 2 html trees in the payload of every storefront document. 27,070 bytes are reachable only through the unused not-found copy on each of four captures re-run today (38.9% of the payload on /s/demo/no/om-oss, 31.6% on the home, 33.4% on a product page, 26.6% on /products); written into the document the copy is 30,688 bytes. /om-oss is 110,507 bytes to show a page whose own markup is 1,583. The header, footer and menus are drawn twice per render, and the cart count is asked 2 to 4 times. Not measured on a store with a builder-made header and footer, which is every store started from a theme: production's demo home is 203 KB against 138 KB locally.
measures.target_a: 1 html element in the payload and under 2,000 bytes of identical payload rows, on every budgeted document, the themed store's four pages included. /s/demo/no/om-oss at most 80,000 bytes raw (79,819 by the sum once the copy leaves, about 78,000 with each sheet drawn once). Home at most 112,000 (107,835 by the sum). 1 cart count per render. Each budget is the first measured figure plus 5%, never above these numbers.
measures.how_measured: e2e/performance.spec.ts: the html elements the inline payload opens, the bytes of identical payload rows and the document's length, on the 5 routes of step 1.3 and the themed pages of step 1.6. Step 2.2 adds the first two assertions for /s/demo/no only; the done-when shortfall widens them. The cart count: the unit test of step 0.22.

measures.name: Page documents read for anything but drawing or rewriting that page
measures.today: listPublishedPages has 35 calls on 37 lines in 22 files, and no limit. Production: 29 whole documents a call, 79,778 calls, 781 s in 78 days. 45 of the demo store's 261 built entries keep the whole list, 117,432 bytes (re-run today on the build). The admin's lists read 2 documents a page at 16 call sites. The knowledge job reads about 40 pages a call every five minutes. Menu titles and the modal check open every published document (57,930 and 68,878 calls). A grid of pages reads up to 48 documents for its cards. The feed reads every article of a blog to print 50. By a rough scan about 20 statements in 17 files select the document of several pages; the findings name 5.
measures.target_a: A cold render reads the documents it draws: at most 3 on a home, a built page or a product page (the page or the product layout, the header, the footer), plus one for a page under an A/B test. 0 documents for a title, an address, a flag, a menu, the modal check, a card that has an excerpt, an admin list, a picker or an idle knowledge run. 0 built entries keep a list of page documents. One cached copy of a product layout per store. listPublishedPages on at most 3 lines (37 today). Every statement left that selects the document of more than one page is named in the ratchet's baseline with its reason (a copy, a translation, a scan of every body), and has a limit where it draws.
measures.how_measured: Today: rg, pg_stat_statements and the scratch script work/pmplan/rdcall.mjs on the build. After the steps: the ratchet's count of statements that select a whole page document (step 1.3), and the tests of steps 0.27, 2.16 and 2.17. Three checks are shortfalls: the named list, a build check for entries that keep a page list, and an integration test that counts page documents per cold render with the counter of step 1.9. In production: none of the 40 costliest or most-called statements that selects a page document returns more than 2 rows a call.

measures.name: Built pages one publish makes stale
measures.today: 261 of 261 prerendered entries of the demo store carry the one tag pages:{store} (re-counted today from the .meta files). About 55 places refresh it: each publish, unpublish, delete, alt text, translation, scheduled publish and AI page tool. So changing one page's body makes all 261 render again. The alt-text job refreshes a store's tags on every five-minute run that wrote one of its texts, 4 texts a run: about 50 runs in a row for a new store with 200 pictures.
measures.target_a: A publish that changes only a page's body makes that page's own entries stale: 3 of 261 on the demo. Seen as an effect: after such a publish the home page and a product page are still cache hits and the changed page is fresh. A change other pages show (a title, an address, a card's facts, a header, a footer, a global part) stays store-wide. The alt-text job: at most 1 store-wide refresh over 10 runs that write (10 today). A fact the scope rule missed is stale for at most an hour: a list that still opens a document for a card keeps the one-hour expiry when step 2.15 gives other reads a week.
measures.how_measured: Today: the build's .meta files and rg. After step 2.14: its unit tests of the save action and the alt-text route, and the scope cases in src/server/pages.int.test.ts. The effect needs two checks no step carries (shortfall): an e2e in the signed-in suite that publishes a body-only change and reads x-nextjs-cache on two other pages (Next 16.4.3 sends that header), and the build check's count of entries that carry one page's own tag.

measures.name: Rows read to find one owner's pages
measures.today: 'store_id is not distinct from $1' cannot use the index: a Seq Scan removes 59,973 rows to return 27 on a test table of 2,000 owners with 30 pages each. 122 uses in 40 files of src/server, and none elsewhere in src or in the migrations (re-counted today). Production: 199,789 sequential scans of commerce.pages read 202 M rows in 78 days, on a table of 1,389 rows.
measures.target_a: Every read of an owner's pages touches only that owner's rows, for a store and for Kaizena Flow's own (store_id is null): an index scan, 27 of 27, shown for the page list, the page by address, the page names and the modal statement. At most 3 uses of the old wording are left, each column against column with a comment. A new use fails the ratchet.
measures.how_measured: The plan test on a seeded table and the per-file count in src/server/ratchet.baseline.json, both made by step 0.23. Production's seq_tup_read for commerce.pages is watched once the table is large; at 1,389 rows the planner may still choose a scan, so the test is the hold.

measures.name: Parts of a built page sent twice, on pages shaped like real ones
measures.today: A product grid with Filter and sort: each of 9 products is 18 times in the markup and 18 in the payload on /s/demo/no/products (170,329 bytes); the streamed second copy is 16,702 bytes of 55,163 bytes of markup. The 1,760-byte breakpoint sheet is in the payload once per row and twice with the layout: 3 times on the one-row demo page, and about 10.7 KB raw of repeated style text on Orbit's six-row home (computed, not rendered). No rendered figure exists for a page of more than 2 blocks, or for a themed store.
measures.target_a: Each grid item once in the markup and once in the payload. Each fixed sheet twice per document, whatever the number of rows: once in the HTML and once in the payload React sends with it. /s/demo/no/products at most 120,000 bytes raw with the layout sent once (114,941 by the sum). A six-row, 31-block page made from Orbit's home, and the themed store's home, product page, listing and built page, each hold a document, a payload and a main-element length within 5% of the first figure, lowered by each change that removes something.
measures.how_measured: e2e/performance.spec.ts (step 1.3 adds the six-row page, step 1.6 the themed store, step 2.3 the count of each sheet's href) and the once-only assertion in e2e/listing.spec.ts (step 2.12).

measures.name: What reading and drawing a stored page loads and runs on the server
measures.today: Three stored shapes are accepted, and six source files and the seed still write the old grid shape (rg today). Each read runs the editor's whole schema: 0.80 to 0.93 ms for a theme's home of 10.5 to 13 KB, at 73 call sites; the schemas take about 35 to 40 ms to build, once per cold instance (an indicative figure). src/server/pages.ts reaches 1,307 source files; the three imports a reader needs reach 104 (re-run today). The renderer, page-article.tsx, reaches 1,396: the page writer, the AI manager's tools, 7 signature theme files (230 KB of source) and 135 files of admin words among them. With pages.ts taken away it still reaches 1,392. A stored page is lean, 10,549 bytes for Orbit's 31 blocks, and no test holds that.
measures.target_a: One stored shape: 0 documents differ from their parse on a fresh seed and on production, no theme, content pack or seed writes an old shape, and no upgrader is left in src. The page reader reaches at most 130 source files. The renderer reaches no page writer (src/server/pages.ts), no design-presets.ts, no page-ai.ts, no AI tool and no signature theme by static imports; its megabytes are the server area's bar (4.0 MB for a storefront page). Orbit's home at or under 11,100 bytes as stored. The parse stays: at most 1 ms for a theme's home and, by the second measure, at most 3 documents on a cold render.
measures.how_measured: scripts/page-shapes.mjs (step 3.17 writes it), the graph test of step 1.8 with forbidden lists for the reader and the renderer (step 2.21 names the reader only: shortfall), and a unit test of the stored size (step 1.6). The parse time is a bench (work/pm/bench.mjs), not a held test.

bar_in_a_sentence: A built page is sent once and read once: one layout, each part once in the HTML and once in React's payload, only the documents it draws and only the scripts of the parts on it. A publish redraws that page alone, every owner's read stays inside that owner's rows, and tests on pages shaped like real stores' hold each figure.
can_the_steps_reach_a: Yes, and no answer of yours stands in the way. Two steps were added: the themes, packs and seed write today's page shape before opening (0.46), and a store page's first scripts are held by name (1.27). The rest was proof: the done-whens of steps 2.14 and 2.17 and eight others now check the bar's own numbers.
tolerated: React sends a server-drawn tree as markup and again as payload: 66 to 71% of a store document is that payload. It is the framework's and stays.
Each fixed style sheet is in a document twice, once in the HTML and once in the payload: 1,760 and 1,814 bytes each on the demo.
Rows' own part sheets may repeat shared rules: at most 2 KB raw on Orbit's six-row home (4,982 bytes as six sheets against 3,071 as one), until step 2.3 draws one sheet a page.
Under 2,000 bytes of identical rows in a payload: the router keeps the store's 404 words (919 bytes today).
A filtered listing still carries the built grid, hidden: about 17 KB of markup for 9 products, paid only by a shopper who filters.
A change other pages show (a title, an address, a header, a footer, a global part, a card's facts) still makes every built page of the store stale: 261 of 261 on the demo.
A person saving an alt text in the media library still refreshes the whole store: one press, not a job.
A fact the scope rule missed can be an hour old on another page.

Every uncached read runs the schema: at most 1 ms for a theme's home, at most 3 documents a cold render. The page model's schemas are built once per cold instance, 35 to 40 ms; the server area's cold-start figure holds that.
A page's document holds its texts in every language of the store, and a render in one language reads them all.
A page keeps up to 50 whole versions with no age rule: 642 versions and 5.4 MB in production today.
At most 3 uses of 'is not distinct from' on store_id, each column against column with a comment.
No test proves that each of the 197 stored settings has a reader; a token scan found none without one.
130 KB of words inline in the editor at first paint, about 40 KB compressed, by decision D540: no screen waits for its words.
owner_choices: Should the builder's palette show each of these near-twins as one entry, with the second as a switch: FAQ and accordion, button and dual button, email form and newsletter? Yes or no per pair. Nothing stored changes either way, and no visitor, request or build pays for the second entry.

After a publish that changes only a page's body, another page that shows something of it which the rule missed can be up to an hour old. Is an hour acceptable? The other choice is that every publish goes on redrawing the whole store.
A page keeps its newest 50 versions with no age limit (642 versions, 5.4 MB today). Keep it so, or also drop versions older than a period you name?
closed_shortfalls: 1. Whole documents are still read where a field would do. TIGHTENED: step 2.17 carries it; the text or done-when of step 0.24 changed with it.

2. Two targets rest on a scratch script. '0 built entries keep the page list' (45 of 261 today) and '3 of 261 entries per page' are read by work/pmplan/rdcall.mjs and by hand from the .meta files. TIGHTENED: step 1.11 carries it; the text or done-when of steps 0.1, 0.24, 2.14 changed with it.

3. Step 2.14 proves a call, not the effect. Its unit test stubs next/cache; nobody replays a publish against built pages (the finding says so: confidence medium). TIGHTENED: step 2.14 carries it; the text or done-when of step 2.15 changed with it.
4. A byte budget cannot see a part of 5 to 20 KB. ADDED: new step 1.27, 'Hold by name what a store page's first scripts may hold'.
5. The old page shape is still being written, and the fix waits until phase 3. ADDED: new step 0.46, 'Make the themes, the content packs and the seed write today's page shape'.
6. Ten done-whens are weaker than the bar or than their own sums. TIGHTENED: step 2.2 carries it; the text or done-when of steps 0.16, 0.23, 1.6, 2.3, 2.10, 2.12, 2.14, 2.21, 3.17 changed with it.
